name: Neru Fragment
summary: At Whelgar's Excavation in the Wetlands, the Neru Fragment preserves part of the Goaz Stone's ancient Titan script. Its words tell of Azeroth's primeval history.

sections.title: Piece of the Goaz Stone
sections.body:
Prospector Whelgar led the dwarven expedition that found the Goaz Stone. The relic broke into four pieces: Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru. Then raptors overran the dig and halted the work. The Neru Fragment remained beneath loose soil among the aggressive beasts.

Once recovered, the fragment can join the others to restore the tablet. The surviving words speak of a divine plan and a doomed prophecy. Dwarven scholars have a record to decipher.

sections.title: Reading the Restored Tablet
sections.body: Prospector Whelgar restores the Goaz Stone once all four fragments are gathered. He continues translating its Titan script. The newly legible words tell of Old Gods chained beneath the land.

faq.answer: The Neru Fragment is a stone piece broken from the Goaz Stone, a larger relic. The dwarven expedition uncovered it in the Wetlands before raptors overran the dig.
The Neru Fragment lies scattered in Whelgar's Excavation, east of Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. It is typically buried under loose soil or hidden among abandoned artifacts.

faq.q: What happens when all four fragments are gathered?
aliases: what does the goaz stone say
faq.answer: After all four fragments are gathered, Prospector Whelgar pieces the Goaz Stone back together and continues translating its Titan script. He pursues the mystery hinted at by the surviving text.

angles.text: For the Explorer's League, recovering tablet pieces like the Neru Fragment helps uncover Titan secrets and piece together the origins of dwarven kind.
